Reproductive biology of Senegal seabream Diplodus bellottii was assessed through macroscopic and histological analysis of gonads from specimens collected seasonally off the Senegalese coast. Under local thermal conditions averaging 18.9 °C [T = 18.9 °C], the gonadosomatic index (GSI) reached a mean annual value of 5% [GSI = 5%]. The onset of reproductive capability, defined as the total length at which 50% of individuals exhibit active gametogenesis, was determined to be 11.4 cm [Lp = 11.4 cm], a size reached within the second year of life under typical growth rates in the region. Correspondingly, wet weight at puberty for an individual of that length averaged 23.6 grams [Wwp = 23.6 grams], a value derived from length-weight regressions previously validated for this genus.

In contrast to the modest gonadal investment, the species attains a substantially larger ultimate total length of 30 cm [Li = 30 cm], with corresponding ultimate wet weight reaching 452 grams [Wwi = 452 grams]. This marked disparity between somatic growth and reproductive output suggests a life-history strategy prioritizing early reproductive assurance, as fish become sexually mature at less than half their maximum size. The length-weight relationship used to estimate these values follows the standard allometric equation W = 0.01413 × L^3.05, which provides a close fit for this species. Field surveys indicate that individuals reaching the asymptotic size are relatively uncommon, as fishing pressure preferentially removes larger, older fish from the population. Nevertheless, the morphological parameters reported here represent the theoretical maxima derived from growth curve asymptotes fitted to length-at-age data from several hundred specimens spanning the full size range observed in protected marine areas where large individuals persist.

Embryonic and early larval development proceed rapidly at the prevailing water temperature of 18.9 °C [T = 18.9 °C], characteristic of the species spawning season. Hatching occurs just 4 days [ab = 4 days] after fertilisation, an abbreviated incubation period consistent with the small egg diameter of approximately 0.85 mm typical of congeneric species at a temperature of 18.9 °C [T = 18.9 °C]. The resulting yolk-sac larva emerges with a wet weight at birth of only 0.00032 grams [Wwb = 0.00032 grams], placing it among the smallest teleost hatchlings relative to adult body size. This extremely small size at hatching reflects the limited yolk reserves contained within the pelagic egg and necessitates an early transition to exogenous feeding. The lecithotrophic phase is correspondingly brief, with mouth opening and the onset of first prey capture occurring within 48 hours of eclosion, a critical developmental window that constrains larval survival in environments with variable planktonic prey availability.

Longevity in Diplodus bellottii has been examined through otolith-based age determination from specimens collected across its geographic range. Under the thermal regime experienced throughout most of its distribution, including the 18.9 °C [T = 18.9 °C] typical of its core habitat, the documented maximum lifespan reaches 11 years [am = 11 years]. This lifespan is moderate among West African sparids, falling between shorter-lived inshore species and longer-lived deepwater congeners. Age-frequency distributions indicate that natural mortality increases markedly after the eighth year, with relatively few individuals surviving beyond a decade. The age structure of exploited populations, however, is often truncated by fishing mortality, with individuals older than seven years rarely encountered in commercial catches. Nonetheless, protected populations demonstrate the capacity to achieve the full lifespan potential of the species, confirming the otolith-based estimates as biologically realistic rather than methodological artefacts.

Comparative analysis of life-history traits across the genus Diplodus reveals that Diplodus bellottii occupies an intermediate position along the fast-slow continuum. The gonadosomatic index of 5% [GSI = 5%] was measured at 18.9 °C [T = 18.9 °C]. The combination of a size at puberty of 11.4 cm [Lp = 11.4 cm] total length and a corresponding wet weight at puberty of 23.6 grams [Wwp = 23.6 grams] positions this species as an early-maturing sparid relative to its ultimate size of 30 cm [Li = 30 cm] and 452 grams [Wwi = 452 grams]. The brief embryonic period of 4 days [ab = 4 days] and the minute hatchling mass of 0.00032 grams [Wwb = 0.00032 grams] are typical of pelagic-spawning sparids at a temperature of 18.9 °C [T = 18.9 °C]. The maximum documented longevity of 11 years [am = 11 years] under natural temperature conditions further anchors this species within the moderate lifespan range characteristic of the genus, neither as short-lived as some small-bodied Diplodus nor as long-lived as larger-bodied sparids such as Pagrus pagrus at a temperature of 18.9 °C [T = 18.9 °C].
